identity.real_world_identity_notes: The Assetto Corsa GTC60 Ferrari 250 GTO entry is a third-party wrapper that loads the official Kunos Ferrari 250 GTO base model; its package documentation does not identify a chassis number or one exact production year. The real-world identity is therefore represented conservatively as the Ferrari 250 GTO 1962-1964 production/racing family, not as a separate GTC60 car and not as the 1964 Series II variant or another 250 GT derivative.

Ferrari's official history identifies the 250 GTO's 1962 presentation, 1962-1964 championship period, 36-car production, and dual road/race purpose. The GTC60 documentation identifies the simulator package as a wrapper around the Kunos Ferrari 250 GTO model, while its year labels are not consistent enough to justify a single chassis-year claim.

claims.basis: Ferrari's official history identifies the 250 GTO's 1962 presentation, 1962-1964 championship period, 36-car production, and dual road/race purpose. The GTC60 documentation identifies the simulator package as a wrapper around the Kunos Ferrari 250 GTO model, while its year labels are not consistent enough to justify a single chassis-year claim.

Ferrari's official technical history explicitly describes the 250 GTO's gearbox as five-speed. Ferrari's official technical history explicitly calls the gearbox all-synchromesh. The secondary transmission description places second through fifth gears in an H layout; it is the only reviewed source that directly states the selector arrangement. The secondary source states that first gear is left and down while second through fifth form the H, establishing a dog-leg H pattern. The secondary transmission description explicitly places first gear to the left and down.
